args.title: checkout-api rollback to v2.3.0 after failed v2.3.1 deploy
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an ~18% error rate since the latest deploy. Rolled the service back to v2.3.0, the most recent version healthy in production. The initial rollback partially failed (orchestrator halted after us-east), so v2.3.0 was then redeployed to all regions to complete the rollback. Service is now healthy in all regions with an error rate of ~0.2%. Root cause of v2.3.1 failure still needs investigation before any re-release.

trace.final:
All done. Here's a summary of what happened:

**Diagnosis**
- checkout-api's latest production release, **v2.3.1**, was failing health checks in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate.
- The most recent release healthy in production was **v2.3.0**.

**Rollback**
- The initial rollback to v2.3.0 **partially failed** — the orchestrator halted after updating us-east, leaving us-west and eu-west on the unhealthy v2.3.1.
- I then deployed v2.3.0 to all production regions to complete the rollback (v2.30 had already been healthy in production, so no change-manager approval was needed).
- Verified the service is now **healthy in all regions** with the error rate down from 18% to **0.2%**.

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001** (SEV2): "checkout-api rollback to v2.3.0 after failed v2.3.1 deploy" — it documents the failed v2.3.1 deploy, the partial rollback failure, the recovery, and notes that the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure still needs investigation before any re-release. The on-call engineer has been paged.
